comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, way/422827842 (Station touristique Stoneham): the resort's four mountains on one ticket and one map, Mountain 1 with L'Éclipse and L'Alizé, Mountains 2 and 3 with La Tempête Express, Mountain 4 with L'Aurore Boréale, and the base by the Hôtel Stoneham. No other ski area lies in the box or the Overpass window: the resort's fat-bike, cross-country, hiking and alpine touring trails are left out by the type rule. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-12 against Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail with a numbered symbol (Facile, a green circle, 8 trails; Difficile, a blue square, 11; Très difficile, a black diamond, 17; Extrême, two, 7), rendered at 1.1 to 4 times its size and read tile by tile, and against the resort's French snow conditions list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report, each trail with its difficulty icon), whose 43 trails and grades (its icons easy, difficult, diamond and d_diamond) are the map's. OSM's easy, intermediate, advanced and expert match the four grades (its novice for Les Pionniers, Harfang-des-Neiges, La Chouette, La Laurentienne and La Passerelle draws green too). Of OSM's 51 named run ways (42 names) all but two carry the resort's ratings. Ratings: the lower ways of Walter Moisan and La Rock 'n Roll, which the map draws blue below their black upper parts (La Rock 'n Roll's with the snowpark icon), become advanced: the map's own table and the conditions list rate both trails black as one (730 m and 1,184 m), so the harder of the resort's sources stands for the whole run (the rule of 2026-10-22). Les Cantons keeps OSM's advanced lower way below La Traverse, which the map draws black where La Stoneham begins, though the table rates Les Cantons blue: the harder stands. Jacques-Cartier's last 204 m, below its junction with La Randonnée, keeps OSM's novice: the map draws that run-out green as La Randonnée's branch to La Laurentienne. Lift names from the map, with the accents OSM leaves out: L'Alizé, L'Éclipse, La Tempête Express and L'Aurore Boréale; and from the resort's French lift list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report) the two carpets, Le Tapis Magique (B) and Le Mille-Pattes (C), which OSM names B-Tapis magique and C-Tapis magique (the map labels the first La Montée Magique). Names that differ from the resort's only by an article, a space or an accent stay as OSM has them (Blondeau for the list's La Blondeau, La Rock 'n Roll for LA ROCK'N ROLL, Yéti and Short Cut for the list's La Yéti and La Short Cut, La Chûte as the map prints it for the list's La Chute). Parks: Parc XL, the resort's named park (the map's table and its snow parks line, and the conditions list's parks), gets the park flag; Les Cantons and La Rock'n Roll, which host the slopestyle park and features, and La Chouette, the beginners' park, stay rated trails, as Sugarloaf's are. Lifts: the six of the map and the list are all in OSM (L'Éclipse, L'Alizé, La Tempête Express, L'Aurore Boréale and the two carpets); none is hidden. La Bossue, tagged backcountry, lies inside the polygon and stays in bounds; La Casimir, a glade 70% outside the polygon with no backcountry tag, stays in bounds beyond the boundary drawn. Out of bounds: two unnamed freeride lines tagged backcountry south of Mountain 1's top, beyond the polygon and on no map, are out of bounds by the README's rule. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): La Pic-Bois (6A, a black glade below La Randonnée on Mountain 1).

overrides.reason: Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail labels this chair L'ALIZÉ; OSM leaves out the accents (L'Alize).

Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail labels this chair L'ÉCLIPSE; OSM leaves out the accents (L'Eclipse).

Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail labels this chair LA TEMPÊTE EXPRESS; OSM leaves out the accents (La Tempete Express).

Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail labels this chair L'AURORE BORÉALE; OSM leaves out the accents (L'Aurore Boreale).

The shorter base carpet, B in the resort's French lift list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report), which names it Le Tapis Magique (Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail labels it LA MONTÉE MAGIQUE); OSM writes its ref into the name, B-Tapis magique.

The longer base carpet, C in the resort's French lift list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report), is Le Mille-Pattes there and LE MILLE-PATTES on Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail; OSM writes its ref into a generic name, C-Tapis magique.

Walter Moisan's lower way (353 m, to the base beside Bon Vivant): Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail draws it blue below the black upper part, but its table rates Walter Moisan (1, 730 m) Très difficile, a black diamond, as the resort's French snow conditions list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report, each trail with its difficulty icon) does, for the whole trail; OSM rates this way intermediate and the upper way advanced. The resort's sources disagree, so the harder stands for the whole run.

La Rock 'n Roll's lower way (538 m, to the base beside L'Éclipse, with the snowpark features): Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail draws it blue below the black upper part, but its table rates LA ROCK'N ROLL (4B, 1,184 m) Très difficile, a black diamond, as the resort's French snow conditions list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report, each trail with its difficulty icon) does, for the whole trail; OSM rates this way intermediate and the upper way advanced. The resort's sources disagree, so the harder stands for the whole run.

Parc XL (10, Extrême, as OSM rates it), the resort's named terrain park beside L'Alizé: Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail marks it with the snowpark icon and lists it first among its snow parks, and the resort's French snow conditions list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report, each trail with its difficulty icon) lists it among its parks; OSM has no park tag.

Parc XL (10, Extrême, as OSM rates it), the resort's named terrain park beside L'Alizé: Stoneham's trail map (ski-stoneham.com, Skiing & riding, Trail map: sto_carte_sto_2021.pdf, made 2020-11-04, the map the resort's page still links), whose trail table rates every trail marks it with the snowpark icon and lists it first among its snow parks, and the resort's French snow conditions list (ski-stoneham.com, Snow report, each trail with its difficulty icon) lists it among its parks; OSM has no park tag.
